scope: The stream chosen before a session: an Index's refresh rate, set in SteamVR for the session, and a Beyond's stream following the mode it is in. What 1.0.0.12's first session on real hardware showed: one parity piece per five video pieces for a wired headset PC, whose path lost packets in clumps; a stop while the rendering PC's SteamVR starts no longer waits out the start; both reports carry the network adapters' drop counters, and the Bazzite client's the remembered GPU clock and whether the session held it from the start; a Game Mode start records where SteamVR's server came from and which display it reached. Every package carries version 1.0.0.13; the native programs are 1.0.0.12's with the new version label and the host's driver is 1.0.0.9's.

from_the_session.what: 1.0.0.12 at Native with eye-tracked foveation on a handheld headset PC on Bazzite, wired, Beat Saber, about nine minutes; from the two reports the maintainer sent.
went_well: the bitrate back at 65 Mbit/s when the GPU clock was held, about a minute in (a fresh start)
no step down for uneven arrival
the add-on warning naming only the headset's own add-ons
about 34 ms from the rendering PC's frame to the headset
put_right: 44 frames rebuilt from parity and 12 lost although every group had its parity: at the loss rate the repairs imply, random losses would almost never put two in one group of ten, and the network test on the same link lost six packets within one frame, so the wired path drops runs
neither report said where packets went missing: on the rendering PC, on the way or on the headset PC

a stop while the rendering PC's SteamVR started waited 88 s: ALVR's shutdown request is accepted but reaches SteamVR only through the headset device of a client that has streamed, and the wait ran to the end of the 90 s launch window
the report did not say whether a GPU clock was remembered or held from the start
Game Mode failed with SteamVR error 496: SteamVR's server had WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0, a name VROSTBridge never gives, and nothing said where it came from
from_the_session.not_put_right: the headset PC's decoder fell behind at 65 Mbit/s at Native and kept up at 55; the bitrate settled between 40 and 55 Mbit/s, as the automatic bitrate intends. The menu button: 0.8 s after the last press the rendering PC's SteamVR re-read the controllers' bindings and 5 s later the game quit, which suggests the dashboard opened; not confirmed, so not changed. Game Mode is not fixed: the new record says why it fails, on the next attempt.
from_the_session.asked_for: by the maintainer after the session: the stream choices before a session (until then they needed a detected headset); an Index's refresh rate chosen there, without SteamVR's menus; and on a Beyond no choice at all, its stream following the mode Bigscreen's Beyond Utility sets on a Windows PC, on Bazzite and Windows alike

changes: host/stream_options.py: FEC_VIDEO_GROUP_WIRED (5): a wired client gets one parity piece per five video pieces, twice the interleaved groups, so a run of lost pieces up to a fifth of the frame comes back (6 to 12 for a 60-piece frame); Wi-Fi and an unreported network keep 10. Clients from 1.0.0.9 take the group count from each parity piece, so they repair either

host/control.py: a stop counts its window from when SteamVR's server appears instead of waiting out the launch window, and quit_steamvr (vrmonitor.exe vrmonitor://quit, SteamVR's Exit VR) follows when SteamVR still runs 5 s after ALVR accepted the shutdown (QUIT_FALLBACK_S); a negotiated restart is left to ALVR

launcher/adapter_counters.py (new): each physical adapter's counters noted when a session starts, and what they gained in the reports (adapter_counters): packets in and out and every drop and error counter that moved; on Linux also the system's UDP receive errors and the stream adapter's driver counters (ethtool -S); launcher/windows_network.py reads them with GetIfEntry2; launcher/app.py notes them on both PCs
launcher/session_tuning.py: the remembered clock (remembered) and the session's use of it (last_session: held from the start, the clock, its raises, set back) in the status and the report

launcher/client_runtime.py: server_origin: SteamVR's server's parent processes, whether it has a mount namespace of its own, the container and Steam variables it was given (names only) and which socket its display name reaches; logged and in the report (steamvr_origin)

launcher/headset.py, app.py, client_runtime.py, session_link.py, graphics_limit.py, game_ui.py and desktop.html: the stream choices before a session, from the last verified headset or, on Linux, a known headset display (known_headset). An Index offers Auto and its Native (2016 x 2240) at 80, 90, 120 and 144 Hz; the chosen rate goes into steamvr.preferredRefreshRate for the session with the stream-only receipt (version 4) and is put back, on both systems, and a rate it did not take is noted (DISPLAY_MODE). A Beyond offers no choice (resolution_fixed) and streams the mode it is in, 2560 at 75 Hz and 1920 at 90 Hz or with H.264 (beyond-90), which only Bigscreen's Beyond Utility switches. A choice the headset does not offer behaves as Auto. Hosts say display-modes; an older one gets 2016 for the Beyond's 1920. When the graphics fall behind, an Index is offered its next lower rate, and a Beyond at 2560 is pointed at its 90 Hz mode
client/transport/lib.rs and tests/transport_smoke.py: the transport's own size checks know all seven stream counters (56 bytes); two were added in 1.0.0.9
